source.title: On the Dynamics of Delayed Generalization in Linear Models
source.authors: Atreya Vedantam; Nataraj Das; Chandrashekar Lakshminarayanan

record.tranche_reason: Reports generalization results under standard training, but does not test the claim versions’ specified interventions or measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper studies delayed generalization in separable linear models and a deep MNIST model. It reports standard-distribution test accuracy, but does not test random-label memorization, the listed architecture/optimizer/batch/regularization/width comparisons, sharpness, or memorized-example removal. Results on the concentrated test distribution concern a shifted distribution and are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes bias dynamics and delayed generalization on separable tasks. Its results do not test any of V1–V8: high natural-label test accuracy alone does not establish V1, and none of the other versions' comparisons or measures is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors attribute delayed recovery in separable linear models to support-vector-driven bias dynamics and slow logarithmic weight growth, and observe analogous output-bias behavior on MNIST. They explicitly qualify that substantial delay depends on boundary-concentrated test data, usual-form grokking is not observed, and their theory does not describe evolving hidden features.
record.recipe_differences: Uses full-batch gradient descent on separable data with exponential loss; studies delayed generalization and support-vector imbalance rather than the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Test distribution: the text reports test accuracy reaching 1 within about 102 epochs on P, while recovery takes about 105 epochs on the concentrated shifted distribution in Figure 1.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard test accuracy reaches 1 within about 10^2 epochs in the synthetic run and stays near 1 in both filtered-training MNIST runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These separable classification setups attain high standard-distribution test accuracy under full-batch gradient descent on exponential loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic concentrated-test accuracy declines and later recovers; support-vector imbalance increases the delay. MNIST exhibits analogous output-bias dynamics while standard test accuracy remains near 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A learnable bias can produce delayed recovery on boundary-concentrated test distributions in separable linear classification, with related bias dynamics in a nonlinear network.

record.problems: The synthetic experiments use a deliberately simple separable setup. The MNIST training set is filtered to enforce linear separability, only the output-bias behavior is analyzed, and the authors report no error bars or repeated-run uncertainty for the empirical metrics.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted concentrated-test distribution results because the prompt specifies that out-of-distribution generalization is separate. Figure-only detailed curve values were not transcribed.

untested.parts: No matched natural-label versus fixed-random-label training, random-label fitting, or random-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep or comparison beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or intervention on local connectivity.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison or tuning-budget comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epochs or adapted training recipes.
No dropout intervention or comparison involving dropout removal.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm and margin measures.
No influence-based memorization measurement or comparison of memorized-example removal with random removal. The MNIST separability filter does not provide this test.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not because the reported standard test accuracies are unreadable. Concentrated-test results are relevant to the paper's distinct claim, but no supplied version covers them. Their omission is already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train the same architectures and recipes on random labels or report chance-level test accuracy for random labels.
No width sweep of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with other generalization measures.
Does not remove memorized training examples.

rows.subject: linear model with bias
rows.stage_stated: trained for 107 iterations; one iteration coincides with an epoch
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on the exponential loss, with no explicit regularization, momentum, weight decay, early stopping, or learning-rate scheduling.
rows.note: The text explicitly reports this result for the standard test distribution.
rows.check: The accuracy result is supported but cannot establish any claim version. Restore lost superscripts: accuracy reaches 1 within about 10^2 epochs, and training lasts 10^7 iterations. This run has no planted support vectors; its fitted maximum-margin separator has a nonzero offset, unlike the theoretical assumption.

rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on exponential loss; all network parameters trained jointly.
